stage: keyframes for 20-25 s social promos of ai-companion outings: Z-Image stills -> human review -> H3 clips -> training/activity_promo.py

canvas.note: Same vertical frame as projects/ai_short_drama. H3 keeps the image's aspect ratio; the cut is scaled to 1080x1920.

style_positive: candid lifestyle photograph, photorealistic, natural skin texture, realistic human proportions, warm natural colours, shallow depth of field, 35mm lens, high detail, realistic lighting
style_negative_extra: anime, cartoon, painting, overexposed, underexposed, crushed blacks, distorted face, malformed hands, extra fingers, crowd, signage, watermark
style_note: First-person point of view: the camera is the viewer's eyes and the character is the only person in frame (the app's keepsake rule: the character alone, never the user). Backgrounds stay uncrowded - passers-by are what H3 changes mid-shot.
lighting_rule: The face is always clearly lit. A night shot names its light source (lamps, cabin light, fireworks) and keeps a readable background.
composition_rule: Each shot has one framing (story.json `framing`: medium = waist up, close = face and shoulders) and neighbouring shots alternate, so a cut never joins two frames of the same size. Candidates A and B are two takes of that framing (subject on the left third / centred). Candidates C / D only after a REGENERATE decision.

extra_compositions.C: first-person point of view, slightly low camera angle, the woman facing right, the story's landmark on the right
extra_compositions.D: first-person point of view at eye level from a little further to the left, the woman facing right, clean uncluttered background

seed_rule: seed = story.seed_base + scene * 10 + candidate_number (A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4).
review_checklist: KNOCK-OUT: not the same face as the reference shot
KNOCK-OUT: a second person in frame
KNOCK-OUT: wrong outfit, or the story's prop missing / present in the wrong shots (story.json props)
KNOCK-OUT: wrong time of day for this shot
KNOCK-OUT: broken hands or earrings, painted text or signage
then choose per boundary, not per image: see boundary_sheet.html
video_potential_questions: Will the face hold when she turns her head?
Are the hands a likely problem?
Is anything in the background likely to morph (rides, lights, people)?
Is the action a single small movement that fits 5 seconds?
age_rule: The promo character is an adult of 23 or older (generate_character.CHARACTERS). The tool never drops the project's age-safety negatives or the cfg 1.5 floor.
boundary_checklist: direction: she faces, walks and looks to the right on both sides of the cut
size and place: her face is not the same size on both sides (medium vs close), but sits in a similar part of the frame
light: one step later than the shot before, never two (compare the brightness and warmth numbers)
the 50% blend - what the viewer sees mid-dissolve - reads as one picture turning into the next, not as two faces
after the clips exist: judge again on last frame vs first frame, because H3 moves away from the still

documentary.positive: documentary-style candid photograph on a full-frame camera, 50mm f/2 lens, natural available light, visible skin pores and fine flyaway hairs, subtle film grain, true-to-life colours, unretouched, realistic human proportions
documentary.negative_extra: airbrushed skin, plastic skin, doll face, over-smoothed, beauty filter, CGI, 3D render, uncanny

phone.positive: casual smartphone photo, slightly imperfect framing, natural skin with pores and small blemishes, mild sensor noise, daylight white balance, unretouched, realistic human proportions
phone.negative_extra: airbrushed skin, plastic skin, doll face, over-smoothed, beauty filter, CGI, 3D render, uncanny

v1.description: a young adult Taiwanese woman in her early twenties with a youthful fresh face and smooth clear skin, long layered dark brown hair with soft curls, dark brown eyes, oval face, athletic build, {outfit}, small pearl drop earrings
v1.negative_extra: outstretched arm, extended arm, selfie, arm reaching toward the camera, hand reaching toward the camera
